_doc: The fish photo judgements (judging/FISH.md, the rubric): python3 tools/fish_judge.py writes them into fish-photos.json (e, jt, c).
photos: teaching id -> {photo id (fish-photos.json f): code}. A code is view (p profile, o oblique, h head-on, t tail, d from above), whole (1, 0 partial),

light (g good: the fish well lit, whatever the background, a flash on black included; d dim: the fish itself poorly lit; n night livery: a night or resting colour pattern unlike the day one; rubric 6, Q308), colour loss (0 none, 1 slight: other colours still visible, 2 strong, 3 monochrome: only blue or green),

clarity (s sharp, m soft, b blurred or murky), size (l large, m medium, s small), count (1 one fish, s several of one kind, o other species with no risk of confusion, k other species one could take for the subject, m the code before that split, x subject unclear),

flags (j juvenile, c camouflage, a out of water), then the ease 1-5. The tool adds the phase flag p for the entries fish.json marks dimorph, and caps the ease (judging/FISH.md "Caps"; the phase flag caps nothing since 2026-11-04).

crops: photo id -> a proposed crop [left, top, right, bottom] as fractions of the photo (curation.json crop's format), when the fish is small in the frame or the margins distract. A proposal for the admin only: never applied by the app or a script.

boxes: photo id -> the fish's box [left, top, right, bottom] as fractions of the original photo (judging/FISH.md "The fish's box"): the tightest box around the whole subject fish, its fins and fin filaments included, for a photo in play whose tags pass the tile rule (tools/fish_game.py tile_tags); tools/fish_game.py cuts its tile from it. A candidate's box is its suggest.json bb.

add: teaching id -> photo objects (fish-photos.json's shape) the pass added for a circle-1 entry short of very easy photos (Pierre, 2026-11-04: at least 5 each): research-grade candidates of fish-cand.json (tools/fetch_fish.py, PR #463: CC0, CC BY or CC BY-NC, the Indo-West Pacific), looked at and judged like the others; only the very easy ones needed were added (to 6 where enough were found). The tool appends them once, by observation.

keep (optional): reference photo id (tools/fish_refs.json f) -> best, alt or dup, for a reference photo on an observation already in play (another photo of it is a game photo): judged against that observation's photos as a candidate is (judging/FISH.md keep); best or alt enters the game, dup stays out whatever the order, of the stopgap list too, and one not judged yet waits (tools/fish_game.py in_play, tools/fish_judge.py add_refs; Pierre, 2026-11-08, Q218). The first ones (2026-11-08, the 17 families of #727): five reference photos of an observation with another reference or candidate photo in play, judged against it.
passes: who judged what, how, and when. A photo of fish-photos.json not listed here is not judged yet (no e: it starts at difficulty 0).
